source_questions.original_text: (a) Outline why a queue is the appropriate data structure to manage print jobs. [2]
source_questions.parent_context:
16. A network is set up with shared printers so that when a user wishes to print, print jobs are
sent to a queue until the printer is available.
(a) Outline why a queue is the appropriate data structure to manage print jobs. [2]
(b) Draw a diagram to show how a print queue may be implemented using a linked list. [3]
(c) Explain why a stack would not be appropriate as a data structure for managing print jobs. [3]
The factorial of the positive integer n, which is written n!, is the product of all the positive
integers less than or equal to n. A stack may be used to perform a factorial calculation as
shown by the algorithm:
//stack for factorial(NUM)
//creates a stack of (NUM - 1) elements
//when NUM = 6
NUM = 6
loop while NUM > 1
stack.push(NUM)
NUM = NUM – 1
end loop
PRODUCT = 1
loop while not stack.isEmpty()
NUM = stack.pop()
PRODUCT = PRODUCT * NUM
end loop
output PRODUCT
(d) Copy and complete the trace table for the algorithm shown for . [3]
NUM = 6
NUM PRODUCT OUTPUT
6
(e) Explain how a stack may be used in the implementation of a recursive function. [4]

practice_questions.question_text: Explain why a stack is unsuitable if equally urgent print jobs must be handled in arrival order.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Choose appropriate stack explicitly scoped. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
practice_questions.solution: Stack pops most recently pushed job first;new arrivals overtake older jobs, reversing desired order and potentially delaying old jobs indefinitely.

practice_questions.question_text: Explain how the call stack supports a recursive function that reduces n by 1 until a base case.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Recursion memory use and stack operations explicitly scoped. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
practice_questions.solution: Each call pushes a frame with local state/return location. Frames accumulate asn decreases. Atbase case returns start;most recent frame resumes first and pops, restoring previous call state until original call returns.
